S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.

subtypes.Loss of Interest: Reduced interest in previously enjoyed hobbies or leisure activities.
subtypes.Social Withdrawal: Reduced interest or effort in social interactions and maintaining relationships.
subtypes.Loss of Motivation: Lack of motivation to initiate or complete work or tasks.
subtypes.Anhedonia: Inability to experience positive emotions such as happiness, satisfaction, love, or pleasure.
subtypes.Indifference to Achievement: Insensitivity or indifference to personal achievements or success.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.

subtypes.Initial Insomnia: Difficulty falling asleep and taking a long time to do so.
subtypes.Middle Insomnia: Waking up frequently during sleep or having difficulty falling back asleep.
subtypes.Early Morning Awakening: Waking up too early and being unable to fall back asleep.
subtypes.Hypersomnia: Sleeping for long periods at night or excessive sleep during the day.
subtypes.Nightmare Disorder: Sleep disturbance caused by repeated and distressing dreams.
subtypes.Non-Restorative Sleep: Feeling unrefreshed despite having slept enough.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.

subtypes.Chronic Fatigue: Fatigue that persists for a long period even after adequate rest.
subtypes.Physical Fatigue: A state of physical exhaustion where the body feels heavy and easily tires even from minor activities.
subtypes.Mental Fatigue: A state where fatigue accumulates rapidly during the process of thinking or concentrating.
subtypes.Loss of Energy: Difficulty performing daily activities due to a decline in energy and vitality.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

symptom.disease_info: Major Depressive Disorder (MDD) is characterized by one or more episodes of at least two weeks of pervasive low mood or loss of interest, accompanied by cognitive and physical changes such as altered sleep or appetite, low energy, impaired concentration, and feelings of worthlessness or excessive guilt, leading to significant functional impairment. The clinical course can be single-episode or recurrent, with episodes often triggered or exacerbated by psychosocial stressors, medical illness, or substance use, though they may also arise without clear precipitants. Diagnosis requires that symptoms represent a change from prior functioning and are not better explained by bereavement alone, bipolar disorder, psychotic disorders, or the physiological effects of a substance or medical condition. Compared to adjustment disorders or normal sadness, MDD is more persistent, more impairing, and involves a broader constellation of affective, cognitive, and somatic symptoms, sometimes including thoughts of death or suicide.

patient.personality: A competitive yet reserved retail supervisor with a sharp visual sense and analytical bent, who finds calm in solitary, detail-oriented hobbies like fishing, photography, and restoring vintage items.
patient.stressor: In the months leading up to his evaluation, Eugene’s store was placed under intense pressure after a new regional manager set aggressive performance targets tied to his long-hoped-for promotion to district manager. He threw himself into redesigning displays, analyzing sales data, and coaching staff, often staying late and sacrificing weekends that he used to reserve for fishing trips and jazz nights, but still saw mixed results and critical feedback about underperforming departments. The combination of mounting expectations and his own perfectionism led him to view every setback as a personal failure, and he gradually abandoned the hobbies and social activities that had previously balanced his work stress. Over the last month, he found himself forcing down quick, joyless meals at odd hours or skipping them entirely during long shifts, noticing that his weight had started to drop, which finally worried his wife enough that she persuaded him to seek professional help.
patient.chief_complaint: “Lately I just don’t feel like eating and I’ve been losing weight without really trying.”

S025.name: Loss_of_Interest
S025.description: A state where interest or pleasure in previously enjoyed activities is markedly diminished.
S025.manifestation: Even on my days off now, the thought of grabbing my camera or heading out to the lake just feels pointless, so I end up sitting on the couch flipping through sales reports on my phone instead of doing the stuff that used to actually relax me.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.
S026.manifestation: Most days lately I have to remind myself to eat something because I just don’t feel hungry, and when I do force down a sandwich in the back room it tastes like cardboard, and my pants are starting to hang looser on me than they used to.

S027.name: Sleep_Disturbance
S027.description: A state where there is a significant change in the quantity or quality of sleep.
S027.manifestation: I lie in bed for what feels like hours with my mind going over numbers and complaints from the regional manager, and even when I finally do fall asleep I wake up a couple of times in the middle of the night and never feel rested in the morning.

S029.name: Fatigue
S029.description: Persistent fatigue that is not relieved by rest and a marked lack of energy.
S029.manifestation: By the time I finish a normal shift now, I feel like I’ve worked a double—just walking the floor and talking to staff wears me out, and when I get home I don’t have the energy to do anything but sit in a chair and stare at the TV.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).
S030.manifestation: Lately, every time a department falls short or a display doesn’t move product like I thought it would, I catch myself thinking I’m useless at my job and that I’ve let everyone down—my team, my boss, even my wife—for not being good enough to get that promotion.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.
S031.manifestation: I used to be sharp with the numbers and layouts, but now I catch myself reading the same sales report line three or four times, and even simple decisions like which endcap to prioritize can leave me just standing there, second-guessing myself.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.
S032.manifestation: On the nights when I’m lying awake, I catch myself thinking it wouldn’t be so bad if I just didn’t wake up the next morning, not that I’ve made a plan or anything, but more like I’m just tired of feeling like this and wouldn’t mind if it all just stopped.
